title: Bishops Clash
transcript: With only one Bishop left per side, it seems like this game is about to fizzle out to a draw, but that could not be further [music] from the truth because if you notice, this black king is a little bit stuck between the white king and this pawn. And so white can actually start with Bishop to F2 check. And now the only move available to this black king is to go to H5. If white wants to have any hope of checkmating this black king, he has to push it to the corner because that's the most likely place for a Bishop to be able to checkmate. So white continues pawn to G4 check. And again, there is only one move for this black king going to H6. And now we have to be kind of careful. If we play G5 check, the king can actually come back down and there is no way to push him to the corner. So white has to play the very cool, calm, and collected king to F6. Now all of these squares are covered, but since this move is not a check, black has the option of playing Bishop to H7, the only other move that is not king to H7, but that cannot be played because actually that would lead to Bishop to E3 checkmate. So black has to keep going up with the king. We want to continue to push this king further up the board. And so pawn to G5 achieves that. All of these squares are covered. These pieces cannot move, so the only move is king to H8. And now we successfully shepherd this king to the corner. But you might notice that it's not actually that easy to checkmate him. If we do line up the Bishop with the king, king can come back to H7. And now we don't really have a checkmate. If we move the king to F5 and we limit the king like this, black can actually now play pawn to F6 and free up his Bishop. If we take the pawn, it's going to get blocked. And if we give this check, still this is not enough to win the game. The black Bishop is going to hold back the pawn. So, we cannot move the king quite yet. We have to find another move. And the winning move is actually to do nothing and just wait around with our bishop. There are some situations in chess where the best thing that you could possibly do is to pass the move to your opponent. And that is called zugzwang. If black could stay in this setup, this would be a draw. But actually, according [music] to the rules of chess, you have to make a move. And the only move available is king back to h8. [music] Be careful. Again, moving the king and giving a check would not be good enough. The king can move out. So, we have to find a very precise pawn to g6, giving up our last pawn. This is taking away the h7 square. But also, black only has two legal moves, either to take the pawn or to move the bishop. If the bishop moves, king to f7 is a checkmate. And if the [music] pawn takes, with only the bishops left, king takes g6 is another checkmate.
